verdict.rationale: Azure documents a cross-platform CLI that runs commands interactively or in scripts, including inside a Docker container, plus REST APIs recommended for unattended DevOps automation scripts. Managed identities supply credential-free tokens, and declarative IaC (Bicep, ARM, Terraform) supports headless provisioning, with a community user noting almost everything can be done via command line. The CI half of the story is only implied, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: explicit CI/CD pipeline integration docs (e.g., GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines), documented non-interactive service-principal login for the CLI, independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Azure CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool for managing Azure resources with interactive commands or scripts.
It can also be run in a Docker container and Azure Cloud Shell.
You might consider using curl in unattended scripts. For example, in DevOps automation scenarios.
Applications can use managed identities to obtain Microsoft Entra tokens without having to manage any credentials.
Almost everything can be done via command line.
